note: Twelve sphere interactions for students who have one loop and need somewhere to go next. Every source URL was fetched and confirmed on 2026-09-10 (see MEDIA_REVIEW.md, Confirmed: Systems Gallery). Field order is fixed so every card reads the same way.

cards.title: The monsoon and the Bay
cards.firstArrow: Hydrosphere (the Bay of Bengal) evaporates into atmosphere.
cards.returnArrowHint: What does the air send back to the Bay, and to Chennai's streets, when the northeast monsoon arrives in November?
cards.signHint: A warmer bay evaporates more; ask what more water vapor in the air does to the heat the bay feels next.
cards.growTo: Geosphere joins first: rain soaks into the ground, or runs off the built surface into the Adyar.

sources.label: NASA Earth Observatory, Historic Rainfall Floods Southeast India (2015)
sources.origin: NASA Earth Observatory, a US government science agency, published this in December 2015 to explain satellite rainfall data from the Chennai floods to the public.

sources.label: UCAR Center for Science Education, What Are Monsoons and Why Do They Happen?
sources.origin: The UCAR Center for Science Education, the teaching arm of a US university research consortium, publishes this page to teach students what monsoons are and why they happen.

cards.title: Reservoirs at zero, June 2019
cards.firstArrow: Hydrosphere (Puzhal reservoir) seeps into geosphere (as groundwater).
cards.returnArrowHint: When the reservoir is empty and every borewell is pumping, what does the ground send back to the city's water supply, and what happens when it cannot?
cards.signHint: Pump more groundwater in a dry year and ask whether the emptier ground refills faster, or dries the land further.
cards.growTo: Atmosphere joins first: a failed northeast monsoon rains less onto the reservoir.

sources.label: NASA Earth Observatory, Water Shortages in India (June 2019)
sources.origin: NASA Earth Observatory, a US government science agency, published this in June 2019 to show Landsat satellite images of Puzhal Lake near Chennai before and after the reservoirs ran dry.

cards.title: Pallikaranai marsh as a sponge
cards.firstArrow: Biosphere (marsh plants and their soil) soaks up hydrosphere (floodwater).
cards.returnArrowHint: What does the stored water send back to the marsh's plants and birds in the dry months?
cards.signHint: Fill in more of the marsh with buildings and ask whether the next flood is absorbed more, or less.
cards.growTo: Geosphere joins first: the marsh recharges groundwater in the rock below it.

cards.title: Coral bleaching, Gulf of Mannar
cards.firstArrow: Hydrosphere (warm sea water) warms biosphere (the coral).
cards.returnArrowHint: What does a living reef send back to the water around it, and what stops when the coral bleaches?
cards.signHint: Push the sea temperature up for a few weeks and ask whether the reef pushes back against that heat, or simply loses the algae that feed it.
cards.growTo: Atmosphere joins first: a warmer atmosphere heats the sea surface.

sources.label: NOAA Coral Reef Watch, Bleaching Threshold
sources.origin: NOAA Coral Reef Watch, a program of a US government ocean agency, publishes this tutorial to explain how its satellite temperature products predict bleaching.

cards.title: Pichavaram mangroves and the shore
cards.returnArrowHint: What does the built-up mud send back to the mangroves that lets them spread?
cards.signHint: More roots trap more mud; ask whether more mud grows more mangroves.
cards.growTo: Hydrosphere joins first: the roots slow the tidal water that carries the sediment in.

sources.label: NOAA National Ocean Service, What is a mangrove forest?

cards.title: Chennai heat island
cards.firstArrow: Geosphere (built surfaces: roads, roofs, concrete) absorbs and re-radiates heat into atmosphere.
cards.returnArrowHint: What does hotter air over the city send back down to the concrete at night?
cards.signHint: Add more concrete and ask whether the air over the city gets hotter, and whether hotter air cools the concrete or keeps it warm.
cards.growTo: Biosphere joins first: trees shade the surfaces and breathe out water vapor that cools the air.

sources.label: US EPA, What Are Heat Islands?

cards.title: Arctic ice and sunlight
cards.firstArrow: Hydrosphere (sea ice) reflects sunlight back into atmosphere.
cards.returnArrowHint: What does a warmer atmosphere send back to the ice?
cards.signHint: Melt a little ice and ask what the dark open water does with the sunlight the ice used to reflect.
cards.growTo: Biosphere joins first: less ice changes where plankton and seals can live.

sources.label: NSIDC, Science of Sea Ice

cards.title: The Amazon's flying rivers
cards.firstArrow: Biosphere (the forest) breathes out water vapor into atmosphere.
cards.returnArrowHint: What does the atmosphere send back down onto the forest?
cards.signHint: Cut some forest and ask whether the rain that fed the rest of it still arrives.
cards.growTo: Hydrosphere joins first: the rain feeds the rivers the forest drinks from.

cards.title: Permafrost thaw
cards.firstArrow: Geosphere (thawing frozen soil) releases carbon dioxide and methane into atmosphere.
cards.returnArrowHint: What does an atmosphere holding more greenhouse gas send back to the frozen ground?
cards.signHint: Thaw a little more ground and ask whether the gas it releases makes the next thaw slower, or faster.
cards.growTo: Biosphere joins first: microbes in the thawed soil are what turn the old carbon into gas.

sources.label: NOAA Arctic Report Card 2019, Permafrost and the Global Carbon Cycle
sources.origin: NOAA's Arctic Report Card, a peer-reviewed annual from a US government agency, published this 2019 essay by permafrost scientist Ted Schuur to summarise what is known about permafrost carbon.

cards.title: Ocean acidification
cards.returnArrowHint: What does the sea send back to the air, and does holding more carbon change how much more it can keep taking?
cards.signHint: Add more carbon dioxide to the air and ask whether a more acidic ocean absorbs the next tonne more easily, or less.
cards.growTo: Biosphere joins first: shell-building animals struggle to build in the more acidic water.

sources.label: NOAA PMEL, Ocean Acidification: The Other Carbon Dioxide Problem

cards.title: Volcanoes and the slow carbon cycle
cards.firstArrow: Geosphere (volcanoes) outgasses carbon dioxide into atmosphere.
cards.returnArrowHint: What does a warmer, wetter atmosphere send back onto the rock over thousands of years?
cards.signHint: Warm the air and ask whether more rain and weathering pulls carbon dioxide out of the air faster, and what that does to the warmth.
cards.growTo: Hydrosphere joins first: rain carries the weathered carbon to the sea, where it is buried as limestone.

sources.label: USGS Volcano Hazards Program, Volcanoes Can Affect Climate
sources.origin: The US Geological Survey Volcano Hazards Program, a government science agency, publishes this page to explain how volcanic gases cool or warm the climate.

cards.title: Water vapor, the loop that amplifies
cards.returnArrowHint: What does the air send back to the sea, and what does the extra vapor in the air do to the heat the sea receives?
cards.signHint: You signed this loop in Step 6 of the tutorial; the source tells you how much it multiplies the warming.
cards.growTo: Geosphere joins first: rain soaks into groundwater, exactly as in the tutorial.
